answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by anchoring identity to an auditable record of real work, not a fresh key: like a voyage counting only after many ports, weight grows solely from months of checkable contributions. A newcomer tends an orchard of tasks whose history cannot be bought overnight, since reviewers verify work and timestamps, so a hundred fakes need a hundred histories. The trellis is non-transferability: weight decays without continued work and cannot be sold, so each fake costs steep time and labour, though newcomers start weak and stolen aged accounts risk abuse until review.
